# rsdoc

> Rust proc-macro that renders diagrams written in doc comments into rustdoc
> output. Supports Mermaid (fully offline), PlantUML, and drawio/images.

Requires Rust 1.71+.

## Install

```toml
[dependencies]
rsdoc = "0.4"
```

## Preferred: the `diagram` attribute

```rust
#[rsdoc::diagram]
/// ```mermaid
/// graph TD
///   A[Start] --> B[Done]
/// ```
pub fn example() {}
```

Recognised fences: `mermaid`, `plantuml`, `image`, `drawio`. All other prose and
code fences are passed through untouched.

## Function-style macros

```rust
#[doc = rsdoc::mermaid!("graph TD\n  A --> B\n")]
pub fn a() {}

#[doc = rsdoc::plantuml!("@startuml\nAlice -> Bob\n@enduml\n")]
pub fn b() {}

#[doc = rsdoc::image!("diagrams/architecture.png")]
pub fn c() {}
```

## Diagrams from files

```rust
#[rsdoc::diagram]
/// include_mmd!("docs/flow.mmd")
/// include_puml!("docs/sequence.puml")
pub fn from_files() {}
```

Paths resolve against the crate root (`CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`), not against the file
the macro appears in.

## Image sizing and alt text

```rust
#[doc = rsdoc::image!("diagrams/arch.png", width = 600)]
#[doc = rsdoc::image!("diagrams/arch.png", width = "80%", alt = "System overview")]
```

Or inside a fence, one `key = value` per line:

```rust
#[rsdoc::diagram]
/// ```image
/// diagrams/arch.png
/// width = 600
/// alt = System overview
/// ```
pub fn architecture() {}
```

## Common mistakes

- The attribute is `diagram`, **not** `mermaid`. A proc-macro crate exports every
  macro into one namespace, so `#[rsdoc::mermaid]` would collide with the existing
  `rsdoc::mermaid!`.
- Mermaid source is checked for: a known diagram type, a direction after `graph`,
  balanced brackets and quotes, and `subgraph`/`end` pairing. Other syntax errors
  do not fail the build — the browser draws an error box instead.
- PlantUML needs either a local `plantuml.jar` (via `RSDOC_PLANTUML_JAR`, or placed
  next to `Cargo.toml`) or network access to plantuml.com.
- Mermaid needs nothing at runtime: `mermaid.js` is bundled in the crate and
  copied into the documentation root during the build.

## Diagnostics

Set `RSDOC_JSON=1` for one JSON object per line:

```json
{"tool":"rsdoc","level":"error","kind":"mermaid","message":"unrecognised diagram type `grap`, did you mean `graph`?","preview":"grap TD A --> B"}
```

Without it, warnings read
`warning: rsdoc failed on `<source excerpt>` (<kind>): <reason>`.

Every diagnostic quotes the diagram it refers to, because a `#[doc]` expansion
carries no usable source location on stable Rust.

## What each source needs

| fence | runtime requirement | output |
|---|---|---|
| `mermaid` | none (bundled JS) | browser-drawn SVG |
| `plantuml` | `plantuml.jar` or network | inline SVG |
| `image` / `drawio` | file on disk | copied and referenced |

For `.drawio.svg`, export from drawio with "Include a copy of my diagram" ticked:
the file then carries both the rendered image and the editable source, so there
is no separate `.drawio` file to keep in sync.
